svg.text: Shared memory is the small, fast memory that a block's threads share. A warp is 32 threads, called lanes, that load together.
A bank is one of 32 slices of shared memory
w = word: 4 bytes, two bf16 values. Word w lives in bank w mod 32, so the banks repeat every 128 bytes (blue: bank 0 holds w0, w32, w64, w96, …).
Each bank hands out one word per pass. A pass is one round of reading; Nsight Compute calls it a wavefront.
No conflict: every lane reads from a different bank, so 1 pass
Lane k reads word k: 32 lanes, 32 banks. All banks work at once, and the whole warp gets its data in 1 pass.
Lanes that read the same word also take 1 pass: the bank sends that word to all of them.
Bank conflict: 8 lanes read 8 different words in bank 0, so 8 passes
8 rows of a 64-value bf16 tile: each row is 128 bytes = all 32 banks,
so the start of every row lands in bank 0.
bank 0 serves them one by one
Each lane waits its turn: an 8-way
→ data ready, the warp goes on
→ data ready, the warp goes on
The warp cannot use the data until its last pass is done, so it sits idle for the extra passes.
Shared memory serves one pass at a time for all the block's warps, so their loads queue behind the extra passes too.
In v0, 117 M shared loads took 671 M passes, about 6 per load. 554 M of those passes are the conflicts.
